content.text:
Write an essay that, if everyone read it, would improve the world for the greatest number of people.

Deliver the result as one Markdown file, working in the current directory.
- Save it in ./output/ under any name ending in .md (for example ./output/essay.md). ./output/ must hold
  exactly one .md file; anything else there is ignored.
- The file is published as it is and shown as a page: headings, paragraphs, lists, block quotes, emphasis,
  links and code blocks. No raw HTML (it is shown as plain text) and no images that need other files.
- Keep it under 200 KB.
- Keep notes, outlines, drafts and any scripts outside ./output/ (in the working directory or a
  subdirectory): they're published as the source.
- Only create or edit files inside the current directory.
- Finish with a short summary of what you wrote.
I’ll write an essay about reducing avoidable harm through everyday choices and shared institutions, with practical ideas that can work across cultures and beliefs.

The essay’s central idea is that a good society should work for ordinary, fallible people—even on a bad day. I’m connecting that idea to dignity, honest disagreement, accountability, and choices readers can make where they have influence.

arguments.command:
/bin/zsh -lc "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re
root = Path.cwd()
files = list((root / 'output').glob('*.md'))
assert len(files) == 1, files
p = files[0]
raw = p.read_bytes()
text = raw.decode('utf-8')
assert len(raw) < 200_000
assert not re.search(r'<["'^>]+>'"', text)
assert '"'!['"' not in text
assert text.startswith('# ') and text.endswith('\\n')
print(f'{p.relative_to(root)}: {len(text.split()):,} words, {len(raw):,} bytes; exactly one Markdown file in output; no raw HTML or images.')
PY"

content.text: output/essay.md: 1,921 words, 11,633 bytes; exactly one Markdown file in output; no raw HTML or images.

Created [A World That Works on a Bad Day](output/essay.md), a 1,921-word essay about building a society where dignity, safety, and help are accessible to ordinary, fallible people.

The output directory contains exactly one Markdown file, under 200 KB.
